 JUDGMENT Parents of deceased Pavan Kumar M.N. filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents, who are the insurer and driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 alleging that on 24.08.2017 at 5.30 p.m., when Pavan Kumar traveling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 on Bangalore - Mangalore road, NH-75 near Adiga's Hotel, Shanthi Grama, Hassan Dist., driver of the Car namely Karthik drove the same negligently made the Car to turn turtle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Pavan Kumar.
2. Immediately after the accident Pavan Kumar has been shifted to N.D.R.K. Hospital, Hassan,
wherein Pavan Kumar succumbed to those injuries.
3. As on the date of accident, Pavan Kumar being aged about 25 years, used to earn Rs.14,000/p.m.
by working as Supervisor at M/s.Magna Info Tech, Bellanduru Gate, Bangalore.
4.

sentences.text: Regarding accident Shanthigrama police registered crime No.126/2017.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1, Insurance Company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement admitting the subsistence of policy with respect to Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202, however denied maintainability of the claim of the petition on the ground that petitioners are the parents of Pavan Kumar, insured/owner of Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202.
6. In the written statement, respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Pavan Kumar.
7. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 appeared through his Advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

8. On the basis of the pleadings on 18.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove

that on 24.08.2017 at about 5.30 p.m. on Bengaluru -
Mangalore road, NH-75, near Adiga's Hotel (Shanthigrama village), Hassan taluk, in view of the negligent use of the Car bearing No.KA-02- MF-6202 accident taken place resulting in the death of Pavan Kumar M.N., S/o.Nagaraj?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

9. On 21.10.2024 petitioner No.1 - Nagaraj deposed as P.W.1 and produced 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16.
On 22.11.2024 petitioners produced evidence of Vijay Kumar as P.W.2.
On 18.12.2024 respondent No.1 Insurance Company produced the evidence of an officer as R.W.1 and produced 2 documents at Ex.R.1 and R.2.

10. Learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners filed Notes of arguments along with xerox copy of the policy pertaining to Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 and Page No.173 to 177 of Motor Accidents & Claims Journal.
11. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

12. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 ...
Compensation is assessed at Rs.18,44,658/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 13. Issue No.1:- In the evidence affidavit P.W.1- Nagaraj stated that on 24.08.2017 when Pavan Kumar was travelling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 along with his friends on NH-75, Bangalore - Mangalore road, near Adiga's Hotel at 5.30 p.m., respondent No.2 Karthik Kumar negligently drove the car made the Car to turn turtle, fell into a ditch, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Pavan Kumar.

14. P.W.1 stated that, immediately after the accident Pavan Kumar has been shifted to N.D.R.K.
Hospital, Hassan, wherein Pavan Kumar succumbed to those injuries.
15. In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
16. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that he never witnessed the accident.

17. In the evidence affidavit P.W.2 - Vijay Kumar, S/o.Suresh, one of the inmates of the car stated that, on 24.08.2017 at 5.30 p.m. when himself, Pavan Kumar and others were traveling by sitting in a Car, driven by Karthik Kumar on NH-75, Bangalore - Mangalore road, near Ranganathapura Gate,
Shanthigrama, Karthik Kumar lost control over the car, therefore car became turn turtle, thereby caused accident, resulting in injuries to Pavan Kumar and others.
18.
In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated that, he was sitting on the front left seat of the car, in the accident suffered fracture of right collar bone.
P.W.2 stated that Pavan Kumar was sitting on the middle of the back seat of the Car, Sowmya and Kavya are sitting on the either side of Pavan Kumar.

sentences.text: P.W.2 stated that he has not filed complaint about the accident and he deposed evidence in the court located at Hassan.

19. In the evidence affidavit R.W.1 Officer of the Insurance Company an hearsay witness of the incident stated about maintainability of the petition by the petitioners, who are the parents of Pavan Kumar (owner/insured of the car).
20.
In the cross examination R.W.1 submitted lack of personal knowledge about the incident.

21. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.126/2017 registered by Shanthigrama police on 25.08.2017 against respondent No.2 Karthik, driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337 of IPC on the basis of complaint presented by Nagaraju S/o.Shivanna - P.W.1.

Ex.P.3 is the copy of 2nd complaint filed by P.W.1 Nagaraju, S/o.Shivanna to Shanthigrama police about the death of Pavan Kumar in the hospital.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar with sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of P.M. Report.
Ex.P.7 is the copy of Inquest Mahazar.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of Charge sheet filed by Shanthigrama police in Crime No.126/2017 against respondent No.2 Karthik Kumar, S/o. Doreswamy, driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
22.
In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 24.08.2017 at 5.30 p.m., when Pavan Kumar and others were traveling by sitting in a Car bearing No.KA-02- MF-6202 on Bangalore - Mangalore road, NH-75 near Adiga's Hotel, Shanthi Grama, Hassan Dist., within the limits of Shanthigrama police station, respondent No.2 Karthik negligently drove the car, made the Car to turn turtle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Pavan Kumar, who succumbed to those injuries at N.D.R.K. Hospital, Hassan.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

23. Issue No.2: In the evidence P.W.1-Nagaraju, S/o.Shivanna, father of Pavan Kumar stated that as on the date of accident Pavan Kumar being aged about 25 years, used to earn Rs.14,000/- p.m. by working as Supervisor at M/s.Magna Info Tech, Bellanduru Gate, Bangalore and used to contribute entire income to the family.
24. In the written statement respondent No.1 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased.

25. In the cross-examination P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident, Pavan Kumar neither worked as Supervisor at Magna Infotech, nor earned Rs.14,000/- p.m.
26.
In the evidence affidavit, P.W.2 - Vijay Kumar S/o.Suresh and R.W.1 Officer of Insurance Company stated nothing regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased.

sentences.text:
In the Driving Licence and Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.10 and Ex.P.13, date of birth of Pavan Kumar is noted as 25.06.1993.
28.
Aadhar card shows that petitioners are the parents of Pavan Kumar.
29. True copy of statement of Account of ICICI Bank marked at Ex.P.9 pertaining to A/c No.272601505776 shows the transactions made by Pavan Kumar from 01.05.2015 to 30.09.2017.
In the file there are no direct documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of Pavan Kumar.

Hence, I have inferred that, it is fit and proper to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of incident Pavan Kumar being aged about 24 years, used to earn approximately Rs.11,000/- p.m. by working in a private company, Bengaluru by adding 40%
as future prospects and by deducting 50% of his income towards personal expenses and by applying multiplier '18', in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Pavan Kumar as - 24 years on the date of accident - Monthly income as on the date of - Rs.11,000/- incident Add: 40% towards future prospects - Rs.15,400/- (11,000/- + 4,400/- = 15,400/-)
Less: 50% towards personal expenses - Rs.7,700/- of the deceased Pavan Kumar (15,400/- - 7,700/- = 7,700/-)

Annual income of the deceased - Rs.92,400/-
 (7,700/- x 12)
 Multiplier Applicable - 18  Loss of dependency =92,400 x 18 - Rs.16,63,200/-
30.

Hence, I assess compensation under the head of loss of dependency at Rs.16,63,200/-, under the head of loss of estate at Rs.15,000/-, under the head of funeral expenses at Rs.15,000/-, under the head of loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 2 at Rs.80,000/- at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each.
Medical bills shows that petitioners spent Rs.66,458/- towards treatment charges of Pavan Kumar.
Hence, I assess compensation under the head of treatment charges at Rs.66,458/- and towards, attendants and conveyance charges at Rs.5,000/-.
Sl . No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1. Loss of dependency 16,63,200-00 2. Loss of estate 15,000-00
3. Funeral expenses 15,000-00 Nagaraj vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16591162/
5 4. Loss of Consortium to 80,000-00 petitioners No.1 & 2 at Rs.40,000/each 5.
Treatment charges 66,458.00 6.
Attendant charges, 5,000.00 conveyance Total: 18,44,658-00 31.
Hence, I assess total compensation at Rs.18,44,658/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.

32. Issue No.3: Regarding liability: In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners by relying on the page No.173 to 177 of Motor Accidents and Claims Journal, copy of the package policy pertaining to Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 marked at Ex.R.2 submitted that respondent No.1 - Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, who are the parents of the deceased Pavan Kumar, who was the insured and owner of the car.

33. In the lengthy argument learned advocate appearing for the Insurance Company by analyzing the evidence available in the file, especially relationship between petitioners and Pavan Kumar who was the insured and owner of the car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 submitted that, petition is not maintainable and in the petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act, before this authority,
petitioners

are not entitle to receive compensation by relying on the following judgments:
1. ACJ 2005-1 (Dhanaraj -Vs- New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and another) D.D.

35. Copy of the policy shows that respondent No.1 - Insurance Company collected Rs.15,264/- as premium and in the policy personal accident covers for Owner/Driver at Rs.2,00,000/-.
36. According to Section 166 of IMV Act, 3 rd parties can claim compensation before this authority - Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: As referred above, in this case petitioners being parents of Pavan Kumar are the legal representatives of Pavan Kumar - owner & insured claiming compensation from the respondent No.1 insurer and respondent No.2, who was the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 owned by Pavan Kumar.
Hence, under Section 166 of IMV Act, under policy marked at Ex.R.2, the petitioners are not entitle to claim compensation before MACT.
However, under other provisions of law, petitioners may entitle to receive compensation before other authorities.
Hence, I came to conclusion that positioners are not entitle to receive compensation under Section 166 of IMV Act.

Hence, I answer Issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act by the parents of Pavan Kumar, who was the owner and insured of Car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202, from the respondents, who are the insurer of the car and driver of the car bearing No.KA-02-MF-6202 is hereby rejected.

transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 7th day of April, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bangalore.
